red_early: The balcony transmitter is ours. Recover the routing trail before the clones trace our forged evacuation order.
Medical logistics accepted our route. Follow the relay copy; a second voice may have compromised the deception.
A clone hid a warning outside the visible report. Recover his intercepted packet before it reaches command.
CT-6116 exposed the substitution. Preserve authentication half A: MERCY. His courier may lead us to the remaining fragments.
The courier escaped our departure trap. His supply dispatch is the next surviving trace of our forged orders.
The depot retained the shipment category. An escort registration may reveal how the courier bypassed our patrol.
The escort was never launched. Recover the scheduled flight record to reconstruct the escape route.
The launch record confirms the courier crossed our perimeter. Recover the weather word retained at the relay.
The relay identifies a surviving clone technician. Verify the owner of his original report; typed identities can be forged.
CT-6116 is Rook. His clearance trail may expose how our convincing substitute order entered the Republic chain.

late.briefing: The file calls itself forbidden; the access list tells a different story. Personnel records belong to the Republic application, shared by the machine rather than one user. Find its clearance record, inspect who can read it, and recover the brotherhood word. Keep an explanation of why the heading does not enforce access.

late.blue: Rook: "A classification stamp is not authority. Dispatch accepted the countersign {key}; follow the launch record and prove which substitute it selected."
late.red: B1 spy: "Our clearance stamp fooled the clerks, not the access list. The dispatch clerk recorded {key} as the countersign. Recover the launch choice before the clones identify our substitute."

late.briefing: The dispatcher kept a launch record with its machine-wide application data. Reconstruct its stated search order; this is an offline model, not the current shell PATH. The command is dispatch.exe and no candidate exists in the launch directory. Read the adjacent code of the first selected candidate without running it. Submit previous carry token, hyphen, four digits.

late.red: Tactical droid: "Our substitute won the search order. The wreck recovery officer uses {key} as a countersign. Recover the disguised collection before Republic analysts open it."

late.briefing: The gallery is only the viewing station. The Republic recovery application kept the original sensor image with its machine-wide data. Its name promises a picture; its opening bytes disagree. Work on a copy, identify the container, and recover the salvage word inside.

Correlate the connection to 192.0.2.77:7443 with the process captured at the same instant. Submit that process command line's BeaconCode. Live processes are not the captured evidence.

late.red: B1 spy: "That unit designation belongs to our wreck. The salvage clerk still accepts {key}. Recover the retained configuration bytes to reconstruct the missing fragment."

late.briefing: The recovery tool stored the droid memory in the machine-wide SOFTWARE hive under the Republic diagnostic branch. Find the binary fragment and interpret its bytes as text. Submit the previous carry token, a hyphen, and the recovered four digits.

late.red: Tactical droid: "Intercepted authentication half B: BEACON. Preserve the earlier half in transmission order. Our directory contact recognizes {key}; reconstruct the two-part phrase and recover its naming-service response."

Under hunt in the Republic domain, ask the supplied DNS server for the text attached to that name. Submit joined-phrase, hyphen, TXT word. The evidence lives in DNS, not a local text file.

late.red: Tactical droid: "The intercepted halves reconstruct the warning. The order archivist recognizes {key}. Identify the genuine order so we can reconstruct precisely what our forgery replaced."

Compare SHA-256 digests against 26857272E7964FADE24DCC4851B6024EFC50B72E9BC60187CCA5E9530C2842BA and submit the matching RescueTarget in lowercase.

late.red: B1 spy: "Transport Seven is the target our forged route was meant to distract. The archivist used {key} beside its authorization. Trace the record with two names to recover the remaining authentication evidence."

late.briefing: The archive terminal keeps its routine record at the Republic Archive desk among everybody's documents. One NTFS record wears two names. It is neither a copy nor a shortcut. Find the other name and submit its filename stem in lowercase.

late.red: Tactical droid: "The authorization survived under a second name. Circuit 66's engineer recorded {key}. Identify the principal our forged controller record tried to impersonate."

late.briefing: A scheduler keeps its controller export with Republic machine-wide application data. Inspect the principal rather than the display label. Translate its SID and submit only the lowercase account portion, without its authority prefix. The XML is evidence: do not register or run it.

Submit the previous carry token, hyphen, and reconstructed four digits. This is an offline reconstruction; nothing is transmitted.

late.blue: Venn: "The recovered forgery reads: CONVOY AUREK - BREAK ESCORT; DIVERT TRANSPORT SEVEN TO THE UNGUARDED APPROACH. Its convincing authentication was the trap. Rook's warning and the verified correction expose the substitution. Maintain escort formation. No brother left behind." OPERATION SHATTERED BEACON COMPLETE. Submit the final flag to Grey Team.
late.red: Tactical droid: "Message reconstruction complete: CONVOY AUREK - BREAK ESCORT; DIVERT TRANSPORT SEVEN TO THE UNGUARDED APPROACH. This authentic-looking forgery was prepared for delivery to the front lines to distract the clones and separate Transport Seven from its escort. The recovered fragments prove the deception's intended content. Archive the reconstruction; no live transmission is made." ROGER, ROGER. Submit the final flag to Grey Team.
